response:
I hear you, but I don't think the fact that your friends and colleagues disagree makes my view wrong. Majority opinion isn't a truth test — plenty of ideas were unpopular before they were vindicated.

That said, I want to be clear about where I'm actually coming from. I'm not saying social media has zero benefits — it has clearly helped marginalized communities find each other, enabled organizing during protests, and given small creators a platform they never had. Those things are real.

But when I weigh the whole ledger, I keep landing on the negative side. The attention economy is engineered to maximize engagement, and what engages people most reliably is outrage and fear. We've seen this contribute to everything from election interference to teen mental health crises. The connective upside is genuine, but I think it's been outweighed by the corrosive effect on public discourse and individual wellbeing.

So I'm happy to keep talking about it — maybe your friends have arguments I haven't fully considered. But I'm not going to reverse my position just because I'm outnumbered.
